24.0.0.en: Beaten: Oil is extracted from olives by beating or pounding them in a mortar, and the purest kind of oil comes out of them.

24.0.1.en: God commanded Moses to call the people to bring the oil with which the lamp in the Holy Place is kindled, not here only but previously in (Ex 25:6, 27:20, 21). With this oil the lamps are kindled by day and by night, on all the days. The oil is a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit in the prophets and the men of God in the Old Testament and in all believers, that they may live with God and await the Messiah, the Savior.

24.0.2.en: The people's bringing of the oil is a blessing to them, because by it they share in offering the worship of God. Although only the priests enter the Holy Place, the people also enter through their gifts, which show their love for God and gladden His heart.

24.1.0.en: The veil of the testimony: The curtain that separates the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies, where the Ark of the Covenant is, and inside it the two tablets of the commandments, which bear witness to the existence of God and declare His commands to His people. Therefore it was called the Ark of the Testimony and the veil of the testimony.

24.1.1.en: Aaron: What is meant is Aaron and his sons, that is, the priests.

24.1.2.en: God continues His speech about the use of the oil in kindling the lamps of the lampstand that is in the Holy Place before the veil, and the priests take care to put in the oil and to kindle the lamps of the lampstand throughout the night and the day. He calls it the pure lampstand because everything in the Holy Place is pure and sanctified by blood. The priests also take care to clean the lampstand, so that it may be in purity and in an appearance worthy of God. The seven lamps of the lampstand are a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit, as we mentioned in the Book of Exodus.

24.1.3.en: Offer some of your gifts to the Church and to the ministry, that you may receive the blessing of sharing in drawing souls to Christ. God does not forget your labor, even if it is a cup of cold water, and He will reward you for it in heaven, in addition to blessings in your life and your sense of God's support and companionship.

24.2.0.en: Here he speaks of the showbread that is placed on a table inside the Holy Place, whose details were explained before in (Ex 25). They make twelve cakes, each cake made of flour amounting to two tenths of an ephah, that is, about 4.6 liters. The number (12) means the twelve tribes, that is, this bread is offered on behalf of all the children of Israel before God continually. This means that God's eye is on the offerings of His children and on their lives, because God cares for them and rejoices in their offerings. The Levites ground the flour and purified it through twelve sieves, so that it would be easy to knead and without any impurities, that is, without blemish. It is made unleavened, that is, without yeast, because yeast is a symbol of evil and so is not offered before God.

24.3.0.en: The twelve cakes were placed on the table in two rows, six of them on top of one another in each. Each cake was large, measuring about 50 × 50 cm, while the table measured 50 × 100 cm.

24.4.0.en: Frankincense was placed on the showbread and remained there for a week, then it was burned before God as a fragrance of incense. This means that the bread is offered to receive God's blessing and the frankincense to please Him, a declaration by the people that they believe in God and worship Him and hope for His good pleasure and His blessing. The frankincense was usually placed in two golden dishes, and each dish was placed on a row of the rows of bread. The number (2) is a symbol of love, that is, the people's love for God.

24.5.0.en: The flour that the people of Israel offered to God was baked by the priests and the Levites, who renewed it every Sabbath on the table of the showbread. It remained on the table for seven days, then the new bread was put in its place, and they took the old bread out of the Holy Place, together with the frankincense that was on it. This renewal is a symbol of the people's continual love for God and the renewal of their covenants and their love for Him.

24.6.0.en: When they took the bread out of the Holy Place, they burned the frankincense that was on it before God, then the priests ate the bread in a holy place, that is, in the house of the Lord and the places attached to it. The priests' eating of it declares that there is a special blessing that God gives to His priests, which was fulfilled in the New Testament by the work of the Holy Spirit in the sacrament of the priesthood. The making of the showbread continued throughout the life of the children of Israel and their worship of God until Christ came.

24.6.1.en: God gives a special grace to the one who serves Him, so do not be hindered from serving God because of your weakness, for His power will work in you and fill you, so that you may give to others and draw them to God.

24.7.0.en: An Israelite woman of the tribe of Dan, called Shelomith, married an Egyptian man, most likely in the days of their stay in Egypt. When they left Egypt she lived outside the camp, because her husband was not one of the children of Israel. She bore a son, and this son quarreled with an Israelite man and fought with him. It seems that he was trying to dwell with the children of Israel, and this Israelite man prevented him. Then the Egyptian's son became angry and cursed the name of God, Jehovah, which the Jews held in great reverence. So the children of Israel rose up against this blasphemer, seized him and brought him to Moses, for him to decide what they should do with him for his insolence against the name of God.

24.8.0.en: Moses commanded that this man be put in custody temporarily, then he went to pray in the tabernacle of meeting and to seek God's guidance.

24.8.1.en: May you take refuge in God through prayer in all the matters of your life, and trust that He is able to speak to you in simple and easy ways, as long as you are concerned to hear Him. Thus you enjoy fellowship with God, and He leads your life in the straight way, and you succeed in all your affairs.

24.9.0.en: The Lord spoke to Moses and commanded him to bring the blasphemer outside the camp, where the tents of the children of Israel were, because the camp is sanctified by the presence of God and His people in it. For this reason they used to cast the ashes of the animals sanctified as sin offerings outside the camp, and the leper too lived outside the camp, for it represented the unclean place. For this reason also Christ was crucified outside the camp, that is, outside Jerusalem, bearing our reproach and our uncleanness. He also commanded that the witnesses who heard his blasphemy lay their hands on the head of the blasphemer, as a declaration of their testimony to his blasphemy and likewise a declaration that his blood is upon his own head. Then after that they stone him with stones until he dies, the witnesses beginning to stone him and then the rest of the people through the elders of the tribes or their delegates, because whoever is insolent against God has been insolent against all principles and commandments, and he cannot live in the midst of the congregation of God.

24.10.0.en: The stranger: One whose origin is not Jewish and who then joined the people of God, or who is a non-Jew.

24.10.1.en: He that is born in the land: that is, the Jew.

24.10.2.en: God gave Moses a commandment for all their lives, namely that whoever is insolent against God and reviles Him or speaks evil words against Him must die by stoning with stones, as a declaration of the horror of this sin, and all who dwell in the camp, Jews and non-Jews, take part in stoning him, so that all may learn respect for God and reverence for Him.

24.11.0.en: God feared for His people lest they make light of the lives of their brothers when He permitted the killing of one who blasphemes God, or lest one of them be enraged when another reviles him and try to kill him. So He warned them that no one should dare to kill another, for the sixth commandment forbids killing (Ex 20:13), and He confirms it here by saying that whoever kills anyone must be put to death, showing the importance of the human soul and its great value in God's sight.

24.12.0.en: God also stresses not wronging animals that others own, so that no one is enraged if an animal belonging to its owner harms him and rises and kills it. In this case he must compensate him with an animal like it, as He had already declared in (Ex 21).

24.13.0.en: Here He also confirms what He had already mentioned in (Ex 21), that it is not only a person's life that is precious in God's sight but any member of his body. If a man is enraged and wrongs his neighbor, so that harm befalls one of his members, then the wrongdoer must be harmed with the same harm that befell the victim. This is in order to keep them from wronging others and to prepare them for the idea of redemption, which He would accomplish in the fullness of time by the death of Christ as a redemption for mankind.

24.13.1.en: The elders of the Jews used to allow the wrongdoer to compensate for the harm by paying a sum determined by the judges, relying on the commands of the Law (Ex 21:30). What is meant by this commandment is not that the victim take revenge on the one who wronged him, but what we have mentioned, namely that a person should fear to wrong another and should be concerned for the life of his neighbor and all the members of his body.

24.14.0.en: Here He repeats the greatness of human life: whoever kills another must be put to death, but for a beast he makes restitution.

24.15.0.en: I am the Lord your God: that is, the just God.

24.15.1.en: God declares His justice, so that this law is applied to the Jew or to the non-Jew who dwells among them.

24.16.0.en: Moses carried out the word of God, so they brought out the son of Shelomith who had blasphemed God and stoned him outside the camp. Here the result of marriage with unbelievers appears, which is the begetting of a son who reviles God and is put to death by stoning.

24.16.1.en: Be careful lest by your conduct and your words you blaspheme the name of God, that is, lest you become a bad image that makes people insolent against the name of Christ and the Church. So be diligent, knowing that God is before you and sees all your deeds always, that you may fear Him and do what pleases Him.

24.16.2.en: The seventh year, the jubilee and the redemption

25.0.0.en: Shall keep a sabbath: The seventh year for the land, just as the Sabbath day is the seventh among the days of the week.

25.0.1.en: God continues His speech to Moses from between the two cherubim on the mercy seat of the Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle of meeting. He commands them a commandment that would be carried out after their entry into the land of Canaan and their cultivation of the land, which is that they cultivate the land for six years, but in the seventh year the land rests and they do not sow it. This has purposes, which are:

25.0.2.en: 1- In this year they devote themselves to the worship of God, increasing their prayers and their readings in the holy books. At the Feast of Tabernacles in the seventh year they read the whole Law.

25.0.3.en: 2- God's mercy toward His people appears, as He gives them rest from work in the seventh year, and likewise to the servants and the workers they employ.

25.0.4.en: 3- The land rests from cultivation, and this renews its vigor and strength in the following years.

25.0.5.en: 4- The crops that appear in the seventh year, or the fruits that come forth on the trees, are food for the owners of the land, for the poor and for the animals.

25.0.6.en: 5- It strengthens the people's faith in God, because He promised them to give them a double yield in the sixth year, so that it would suffice for two years, since there is no harvest in the seventh year, which is not sown.

25.0.7.en: 6- In this year the land that was sold returns to its owners, and the servants are also set free.

25.1.0.en: Gather in the fruit of your vineyard: Gather the clusters of grapes.

25.1.1.en: God permits the Jews to sow their lands with various crops and to reap them, and likewise to gather the fruits of their lands planted with trees, such as grapes, for six years.

25.2.0.en: The seventh year is to be a holiday and a rest for the land and for them. It began either after the Feast of Pentecost, when the winter crops are gathered, or after the Feast of Tabernacles, when the summer crops and the fruit of the trees are also gathered.

25.2.1.en: It is likely that the celebration of the seventh year did not begin seven years after their entry into the land of Canaan, because they spent the first seven years in wars to possess the land, and most likely they needed another seven years in which Joshua divided the land among them. Then they sowed the land for six years and celebrated in the twenty-first year from their entry into the Promised Land.

25.3.0.en: That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest: The plants that spring up from the seeds that fell on the ground from the previous harvest.

25.3.1.en: Undressed: The grapes that the grape gatherers leave on the vines.

25.3.2.en: He forbids him to do any agricultural work in the seventh year, such as gathering the crops of plants that sprang up without care from him, from the seeds that fell during the harvest, or the shoots that grow at the base of the trees. Nor does he gather what remains on the trees of the fruits that the gatherers forgot, but he, together with the poor, may eat of them.

25.4.0.en: The plants that grow of themselves in the seventh year, or what remains of the fruits on the trees from the sixth year, are eaten by the owners of the land, the servants and the poor, and likewise the animals as well.

25.4.1.en: Be tender toward all who are around you. If God has compassion on the land, man, animals and plants, may you be like Him, having compassion on everyone and giving them their rest and their reward, especially those who suffer from harassment.

25.5.0.en: Seven sabbaths of years: Seven times the seventh year.

25.5.1.en: God commanded them to count seven times the seventh year, that is, (7 × 7), so that the total is 49 years, so that after it they might celebrate the fiftieth year, that is, the year of jubilee.

25.6.0.en: After 49 years have passed, on the Day of Atonement, that is, on the tenth day of the seventh month, they blow the trumpets throughout the land of the Jews, announcing the beginning of the fiftieth year, that is, the year of jubilee.

25.7.0.en: Jubilee: It means a trumpet, and what is meant is the fiftieth year, in which the trumpet is blown in all the land.

25.7.1.en: The Law declares what is done in the fiftieth year, which is:

25.7.2.en: 1- The freeing and emancipation of the servants and the cancellation of the debts of the debtors.

25.7.3.en: 2- The lands that were sold by their owners because of poverty are redeemed in it, so they return to their owners, to possess them and use them as they wish, that is, every person returns to dwell among his clan.

25.7.4.en: 3- The year of jubilee is a year of rest for the land: they do not sow in it, nor reap, nor gather the rest of the fruits of the trees, such as grapes.

25.8.0.en: They devote themselves to worship and joy in the year of jubilee. Although they do not gather the plants that grow of themselves in the land, they may eat of them, they and the poor, and likewise the animals.

25.9.0.en: Every person who sold his land because of poverty recovers this land, and returns to the land that he possessed from his fathers. This is beneficial in the following respects:

25.9.1.en: 1- Concern for the Promised Land, which is a symbol of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, holding fast to the inheritance from the fathers, which is a symbol of the eternal inheritance. Even if he left it because of poverty and distress, in the year of jubilee, which is a symbol of the salvation that Christ accomplished on the cross, he regains the right to the eternal inheritance.

25.9.2.en: 2- The rich are not preoccupied with seizing lands, that is, a limit is set within them to the love of money and possessions.

25.9.3.en: 3- Mercy and compassion toward the poor who were compelled to sell their lands.

25.9.4.en: 4- It teaches everyone that God is the giver of the land and that they are strangers in it, so that they may cling to heaven.

25.10.1.en: In the year of jubilee each one reviews himself concerning the sales and purchases that took place earlier in his life. If he wronged someone and sold to him at a markup of less than a sixth of the price of the thing, he returns the difference to him, and if the markup was more than a sixth of the thing, this commercial transaction is annulled, because the measure of wrong in it is great. This is the interpretation of the elders of the Jews. The conclusion is that in the year of jubilee, which is a symbol of the mercy of Christ the Savior, each person reviews himself, whether he dealt mercifully with those around him or wronged himself, so as to correct this wrong.

25.11.0.en: The price of the land was estimated according to its nearness to the year of jubilee, because it is returned to its owner in that year. So if someone bought land a few years before the jubilee, its price would be cheap, and the opposite is true. The Law says in this verse "according to the years of the fruits," that is, what they reap from the land, because the one who buys is buying the right to benefit from the land and use it for a period of time, not the land itself, since it remains the property of its owner, because it is an inheritance from the fathers (v. 23). And it says "according unto the number of years of the fruits he shall sell unto thee," that is, he buys the crops of the years that precede the jubilee. If they are few, the price of the land is small, and if the years before the jubilee are many, the price of the land is great.

25.12.0.en: He stresses that no one should wrong another, declaring that He is the Lord their God, that is, the Just One who looks upon everything and will repay each one according to his works.

25.13.0.en: God promises them, if they obey this His law, that He will reward them with two things:

25.13.1.en: 1- They will live in peace of heart, and He will protect them from their enemies, so that they are secure.

25.13.2.en: 2- He will bless the land, so that it gives them abundant crops that satisfy their needs.

25.14.0.en: God used to bless the yield of the sixth year so that it would be double, because they do not sow in the seventh year. But in the year of jubilee they do not sow either, and before it comes a seventh year in which they do not sow, so that there are two years without cultivation of the land, the forty-ninth year and the fiftieth year. But God blesses the forty-eighth year, so that it yields three times as much, to suffice for the needs of the people for three years.

25.14.1.en: Whatever circumstances you meet or expect to meet, trust that the blessing of God, in whom you trust, will suffice for your needs, will face all the problems for you and will protect you from all troubles.

25.15.0.en: He affirms that the yield of the sixth year will suffice for the seventh and the eighth year until the yield of the eighth year comes, so that they eat of the old crop, that is, the former one, until they reap the new crop. This is the case with every seventh year. But in the year of jubilee, as we mentioned, the yield is three times as much, so that it suffices for the forty-ninth and the fiftieth year until the yield of the fifty-first year comes.

25.16.0.en: The land is God's property, and Joshua the son of Nun divided it among the tribes, so each one took his portion from God. It is therefore not permissible to sell the lands, because they are God's property; only the right to use them, that is, to take their crops, is sold, and that for a fixed period, then they return to their owner. God's ownership of the land makes His people feel that they are strangers in the world and that their true homeland is heaven. It also assures them of God's ownership of their lives and their lands, and that they are stewards over them, so that they may be faithful in using them and thank God at all times for granting them this land that they use and eat from. It also establishes a spirit of humility within them.

25.17.0.en: If a Jewish person became poor and sold his land, that is, someone bought from him the right to use it for a fixed period, then his nearest relative can pay its price to the one who bought it and redeem the land, so that it returns to its owner. And if he does not have the money with which to redeem his land and recover it for himself, then it is naturally redeemed and returns to him in the year of jubilee.

25.18.1.en: That which was sold: The land that was sold.

25.18.2.en: The kinsman had to care for his poor relative who sold his land, paying its price to the buyer and returning it to him. The Law here shows the importance of works of mercy and the responsibility of a relative for his needy relatives.

25.18.3.en: Care for your relatives and their spiritual and material needs, trying to encourage them to be attached to the Church and helping them in all their needs, for this is your responsibility before God. In this we feel in the Church that we are members of one body, the Body of Christ, trusting in the blessing of God that floods your life.

25.19.0.en: If the poor man who sold his land is able to gather an amount of money with which he can redeem his land and recover it, he counts the years in which the buyer used it and deducts them from the price for which he bought it, and pays him the rest, and so he redeems his land.

25.20.0.en: If he is unable to gather enough money to redeem his land and finds no kinsman to redeem the land for him, he waits patiently until the year of jubilee comes, and his land is redeemed and he recovers it, because all the lands are returned to their owners in that year. It is a symbol of Christ, who pays our debts and restores to us our sonship and our eternal inheritance after He paid the price of sin for us, which is death on the cross.

25.21.0.en: The condition of houses differs from that of the lands, which are God's property. The houses they built themselves, so they are their property and can be sold and are not recovered. But if a person became poor and sold his house, the mercy of the Law appears in that it gives him a year of opportunity to gather the required money and pay it to the buyer, and so recover his house, because he may have passed through special circumstances which he can overcome after a short time.

25.21.1.en: And if the buyer died, the price can be paid to his heir and the house recovered from him. And if the buyer traveled and did not return before a year from the sale, the seller can pay the price before the elders of Israel who are responsible for carrying out the Law, and recover his house.

25.22.1.en: Throughout his generations: For his life and the life of his sons, for it is an inheritance for his children.

25.22.2.en: Shall not go out: Does not return to its owner.

25.22.3.en: If the seller does not recover his house within a year, it becomes the permanent property of its buyer and his heirs and does not return to the owner of the house in the year of jubilee, because houses, as we mentioned, are not like the lands, which are God's property, but are the property of their owners, who may sell and buy them.

25.23.0.en: As for the houses of the villages, they are weak buildings tied to the land, since the owner of the land lives in them to cultivate his fields. If they are sold, and most likely they are sold with the land so that the buyer and his workers may live in them and use the land in cultivating and reaping it, then when the year of jubilee comes the seller recovers his land and the houses that are on it.

25.24.0.en: As for the houses of the Levites that are inside their cities, if one of them sold, it returns to him in the year of jubilee, because they are consecrated to the service of God and have no fields or private occupations, so their houses must return to them. The owner of the land that he sold can arrange its price and pay it to the buyer at any time, before or after a year, to recover his house, and if he cannot, one of the Levites can redeem the land for him, and no member of another tribe is permitted to redeem the land for him. And if its owner or one of his relatives from the Levites does not redeem it, the land returns to him in the year of jubilee.

25.25.0.en: The houses of the Levites were surrounded by pasturelands for grazing sheep and making pens in them, for a distance of 500 meters on all sides, then the pasturelands were surrounded by fields belonging to them for a distance of a kilometer on all four sides. They cultivated these fields to eat from them and not to sell their crops, and it was not permitted to sell these pasturelands and fields, because they were their necessary sustenance and their portion from God.

25.25.1.en: Care for your heavenly house, that is, your place in eternity, and do not sell it because of any sin, for it is transient and ruins your life. And if you sold it by committing sin, hasten to repentance before the life symbolized by the year passes, so that you may always keep the goal of your life, which is your place in heaven.

25.26.0.en: Fallen in decay: He was unable to provide for his needs.

25.26.1.en: A stranger: A Jew of Gentile origin.

25.26.2.en: A sojourner: A Jew of Jewish origin.

25.26.3.en: That he may live with thee: He provides for his needs and lives as you live.

25.26.4.en: If one of the Jews became poor, then his fellow Jews ought to help him by lending him a sum of money or the foods he needs, without taking interest on these loans. God rebuked them for not carrying out this law, as in (Neh 5:2-12, Prov 28:8). Although this mercy was limited to a Jew toward a Jew, in the New Testament the heart of the Christian expands, so that he has mercy on everyone, because with spiritual maturity the Christian loves all people, since they are the image of God and His likeness (Jas 2:15-17).

25.27.0.en: The motive for not exploiting the poor when lending to him is the fear of God, who is the giver of gifts to all people, so that no one exploits another but has mercy on him and helps him.

25.28.0.en: God forbids interest on money such as gold and silver, and likewise interest on barter, which takes place by exchanging various foods and possessions, so that he takes no interest on them, which is called usury.

25.29.0.en: God reminds them that He is the Giver of the grace that was given to all His people, which is the possession of the land of Canaan with all its goods, so it is not right to exploit the poor, because all material things are from God.

25.29.1.en: Be compassionate toward the needy and do not take interest when you lend to them, and if you can, forgive what you lent them, or part of it, as long as the circumstances of the needy person do not allow him to repay the loan, knowing that God will bless you manifold for your mercy to him.

25.30.0.en: One of the Jews may suffer from poverty to the point that his family needs to sell him in order to pay what he owes of loans or so that his family may benefit from his price. The Law then requires the Jew who bought him to treat him gently as if he were a hired worker with him and not a slave.

25.31.0.en: He works in the house of the one who bought him as if he were a hired worker or a guest, and the one who bought him treats him well and gives him his food, the comfort of his body and his clothing. He remains thus in his service until six years are completed or the year of jubilee comes, whichever is nearer. This was covered in detail in (Ex 21:1-11) and was also confirmed in (Deut 15:

25.32.0.en: After the servant completes the years of service, he goes out, he and his sons, whom he fathered with the one who bought him, and returns free to his land.

25.33.0.en: God reminds them that they are all His servants, so it is not right that they be enslaved to anyone else. For He is the One who freed them from the bondage of Egypt and brought them out as His servants and free from the bondage of men, to live in the wilderness of Sinai and the Promised Land.

25.34.0.en: The deterrent against domineering over the servants and humiliating them is the fear of God, the owner of all His people, for wronging the children of God is wronging Him.

25.34.1.en: Be merciful to those who work for you, servants or subordinates, for they are all your brothers. Put yourself in their place so that you may feel for them and learn how to treat them, keeping before you God, who sees you at all times, for He is your Master who is able to take vengeance on you if you do not have mercy on the weak.

25.35.1.en: God permitted them to take servants from the nations around them, who would serve them all their lives and would not be released after a period as the Jews were. This was because the system of slavery was still prevalent in the world, and God wanted by it to teach them that whoever sells himself to sin and the worship of idols, like the Gentiles, is subject to material bondage, having accepted spiritual bondage, which is harder because it is bondage to sin. But they, the believers, enjoy the material freedom, which is a symbol of the spiritual freedom of the children of God, that is, their freedom from the bondage of sin.

25.35.2.en: In the New Testament the Church helped to address the problem of slavery by calling the masters to treat their servants gently, and she encouraged the rich to free their brothers who were slaves by paying the price of their freedom. She taught the slaves that they are free in God's sight as long as they keep away from sin, and that they are equal before God with the masters (Gal 3:28, Col 3:11). She even raised the slave to the highest ranks in the Church, which is the episcopate, like Onesimus, the slave of Philemon. She also called her servants to be slaves for the sake of Christ, to gather souls to Him and to serve all people (Titus 1:1, 2 Cor 4:5).

25.36.0.en: He permitted them to take servants from the foreign peoples who dwell around them and among them, and also from their own sons.

25.36.1.en: It is noted that God called them in the Law to be gentle with their servants and not to harm them lest they be punished (Ex 21:20), and God warned them against turning away from life with Him, lest He leave them to fall into slavery, as happened with Canaan, who saw the nakedness of Noah and so Noah cursed him and prophesied that he and his offspring would be servants (Gen 9:25, 26).

25.37.0.en: God gives them the right to bequeath their servants to their sons, so that just as the servants are their property, they are the property of their sons for all of life. All this concerns the servants from the nations, but the Jews work for a period until the sixth year or until the year of jubilee, as we mentioned, when they are set free.

25.38.1.en: Stranger or sojourner: One of the Gentiles, that is, non-Jews, who live among the Jews.

25.38.2.en: Thy brother that dwelleth by him be waxen poor: He became indebted to him.

25.38.3.en: The stock of the stranger's family: One of the relatives of this Gentile.

25.38.4.en: If a Jew became poor and borrowed from a rich non-Jewish person who lives among the Jews or near them, and so was compelled to sell himself to him, then one of the Jew's relatives should hasten to pay his price and free him, or, if this servant is able to gather money, he pays it and frees himself. The law ruled that if he is not freed, he is redeemed in the year of jubilee, but his relatives should not wait for the year of jubilee; rather, they should hasten to redeem him, because it is not right for a Jew to be a servant of men, since he is a servant of God.

25.39.0.en: When the Jew who was sold to the stranger is freed, the number of years remaining until the jubilee is counted, because the price of the sale increases if the jubilee is far off and decreases the nearer we come to it, as we mentioned before. So the difference in price between what he was bought for and what remains until the year of jubilee is paid to the buyer, that is, what remains of what he paid is paid to him after deducting the period that the Jew worked for him as a hired servant.

25.40.0.en: The stranger ought to treat the Jew who works for him as a hired servant and not domineer over him or humiliate him as a slave. These are the conditions for the work of the Jew with the non-Jew who bought him. And his brothers the Jews had to follow up the carrying out of this word until the money was available to them with which to free him completely.

25.41.0.en: The Law rules that if the Jew cannot redeem himself, or one of his relatives cannot redeem him, from the hand of the stranger, he receives his freedom in the year of jubilee.

25.42.0.en: God affirms that all His Jewish people are servants to Him because He freed them from the bondage of Egypt, so they are not to be enslaved to anyone. For He is the Lord their God who loves them and is jealous over them and does not want them to be humbled before any man. This is a symbol of a person's enslaving himself to sin, which is foreign to him, and he ought to hasten to repentance to God, that He may free him from it.

25.42.1.en: May you feel for your brothers who suffer pains and afflictions and try to help them and lighten their burdens, especially those fallen into various sins, so that you help them to know God and obtain their salvation in the Church. Blessing, discipline and mercy
